Selected work

Master's thesis, Öhlins Racing, 2026

Adaptive damper control from driver behaviour

  • 13comfort-related driver behaviours identified from pedal and steering inputs
  • 16trials in each factorial round, over four damper settings at two levels
  • 9drivers in a blind test in Brembo's driver-in-the-loop simulator, Bergamo

Semi-active dampers react to what the car is doing. This thesis, written at Öhlins Racing together with Ted Degernäs, adds the driver. We developed an algorithm that reads throttle, brake and steering inputs in real time, recognises mistakes such as uneven braking or not easing off the brake before a stop, and rescales each damper until the event is over.

We recorded drives of a Tesla Model 3 in Assetto Corsa, exported the telemetry through MoTeC i2 to MATLAB and co-simulated the car in Simulink and IPG CarMaker. The comfort mode was tuned with a factorial test design over the four damper settings, repeated three times per behaviour. The track-driving mode was tested blind by nine drivers in a driver-in-the-loop simulator.

In simulation the comfort mode clearly improved comfort for a majority of the behaviours, most of all in pitch velocity, with smaller gains in longitudinal jerk and vertical acceleration. The simulator study was inconclusive, mainly because the steering feedback was not accurate enough. The identification itself triggered in the right situations.

Read the thesis on DiVA

My part
Algorithm and state logic developed jointly, then lead on post-processing of the results

Co-founder, product development, ongoing

TILQE: designer switches and sockets in metal

TILQE is a hardware start-up I co-founded, backed by KTH Innovation. We develop light switches, sockets and dimmers with a carefully crafted metal design, at a fairer price than the established designer brands.

I work on product development and design for manufacturing. In practice that is CAD in Fusion, fit and tolerance iterations on printed prototypes, FEM checks of the front plates, and preparing parts for CNC machining and surface finishing.

The goal in every decision is the same: a part that can be made reliably and at reasonable cost, without giving up the premium finish.

My part
Mechanical design, DFM, prototyping and supplier preparation
Tools
Fusion, FEM, 3D printing, CNC machining

Race engineer, 2025 season

NXT Gen Cup: four drivers, one engineer

NXT Gen Cup is a fully electric junior touring car cup. In the 2025 season I worked as race engineer for four drivers, side by side with the mechanics in the pit during race weekends.

Over the season my drivers took race wins and podium finishes in several races.

KTH project, powertrain and transmission

Go-kart powertrain and centrifugal clutch

In a KTH project where a team designed a complete go-kart, I was responsible for the powertrain and transmission.

I designed the centrifugal clutch assembly from the ground up in Siemens Solid Edge. That included working out the spring stiffness and installed length so that the clutch engages as the throttle is pressed, but stays open while the engine idles.

My part
Powertrain and transmission, full clutch design

Siemens Solid Edge

Bachelor's thesis, KTH, 2024

Why orthodontic mini-screws break

  • 0.95 Nmmean torque at fracture for a straight screw
  • 0.55 Nmwhen the screw is bent 30°, which is 42 % lower
  • 95 %confidence that a pilot hole lowers the insertion torque

Titanium mini-screws, 9 × 2 mm, anchor orthodontic appliances in the palate. They sometimes break during insertion even when the torque stays within the specified range. Together with Teodor Berg I set out to find why.

We tested screws to fracture in a torque rig, both straight and pre-bent to 20° and 30°, and compared the results with analytical calculations and FEM in Ansys.

The answer was bending. Torque combined with a bending load breaks the screw far earlier than torque alone, so a straight insertion matters more than the torque setting. A pilot hole lowers the torque needed and widens the margin. We also proposed a rounded screw head that is less able to transfer bending moment into the screw.

Read the thesis on DiVA (in Swedish)

Tools
Ansys, MATLAB, physical testing
With
Teodor Berg

About

I graduated from KTH Royal Institute of Technology in 2026 with an MSc in Vehicle Engineering, and wrote my thesis at Öhlins Racing.

The projects on this page follow the same path: model the design, check it with simulation and testing, then build it. That applies to a clutch that has to engage at the right engine speed as much as to a front plate that has to be machined at a sensible cost.

I have also worked as a race engineer in NXT Gen Cup and co-founded the hardware start-up TILQE.
